variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: CLIP (Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training) is a dual-encoder model that learns which images and text descriptions belong together. One encoder turns an image into a vector, another turns text into a vector, and learned projections place both vectors in the same coordinate system.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Treat temperature as a confidence control”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Low scale
pairs.explanation: Softmax probabilities stay flatter. Hard negatives receive less concentrated gradient pressure, but genuinely strong matches may not separate enough.

pairs.label: Useful scale
pairs.detail: The model can emphasize meaningful similarity gaps while retaining enough probability mass to learn from several candidates.
pairs.explanation: The model can emphasize meaningful similarity gaps while retaining enough probability mass to learn from several candidates.

pairs.label: Extreme scale
pairs.detail: Tiny cosine differences become overconfident logits.
pairs.explanation: Tiny cosine differences become overconfident logits. Label noise and false negatives then receive large penalties and can destabilize training or calibration.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. A matching image and text should point in similar directions after projection and normalization; mismatched pairs should point in different directions.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Low scale: Softmax probabilities stay flatter. Extreme scale: Tiny cosine differences become overconfident logits.

pairs.label: Cross-modal retrieval
pairs.detail: Index freshness and vector compatibility are correctness concerns.
pairs.explanation: Index freshness and vector compatibility are correctness concerns. A new image tower normally requires a new image index.

pairs.label: Zero-shot classification
pairs.detail: The resulting softmax is relative to the supplied classes.
pairs.explanation: The resulting softmax is relative to the supplied classes. It is not an open-world probability that the image truly belongs to one of them.

variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Make the trade-offs explicit”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Dual encoder vs cross-encoder
pairs.detail: Independent vectors make catalog retrieval fast and cacheable.
pairs.explanation: Independent vectors make catalog retrieval fast and cacheable. They lose token-to-region interaction that a cross-encoder can use for detailed reranking.

pairs.label: Large batch vs clean labels
pairs.detail: More negatives can improve representation learning, but memory, communication, duplicate pairs, and semantic false negatives grow with the global batch.
pairs.explanation: More negatives can improve representation learning, but memory, communication, duplicate pairs, and semantic false negatives grow with the global batch.

pairs.label: Higher resolution vs serving cost
pairs.detail: More visual tokens can preserve small details while increasing image-encoder latency, memory, index rebuild time, and operational cost.
pairs.explanation: More visual tokens can preserve small details while increasing image-encoder latency, memory, index rebuild time, and operational cost.

pairs.label: Prompt ensemble vs simplicity
pairs.detail: Several prompts can reduce wording sensitivity, but the full template bank becomes a tested, versioned part of every zero-shot release.
pairs.explanation: Several prompts can reduce wording sensitivity, but the full template bank becomes a tested, versioned part of every zero-shot release.

pairs.label: ANN search vs exact search
pairs.detail: Approximate indexes reduce query cost at scale.
pairs.explanation: Approximate indexes reduce query cost at scale. Their own recall, filters, quantization, and freshness must be evaluated against exact neighbors.

pairs.label: One score vs layered decision
pairs.detail: A raw similarity threshold is easy to deploy.
pairs.explanation: A raw similarity threshold is easy to deploy. High-impact decisions need calibration, specialized evidence, policy rules, review, and an abstain path.

variants.prompt: What invariant makes an image vector directly comparable with a text vector in CLIP?
options: Both encoders must use the same Transformer weights.
Both outputs are projected to the same dimension and L2-normalized before similarity.
Every text must contain the image filename.
Both modalities must have the same number of input tokens.
variants.explanation: The towers can have different architectures and widths. Paired projections plus normalization create the common geometry used by the dot product.
